raised_when: nhst_mde is “Not yet considered” or nhst_mde_source is “Not established”
message: The smallest effect worth detecting has not been established, or has no stated basis. Where it is chosen to make an available sample look adequate, the calculation justifies itself.
prompt: Ask what effect would actually change the decision, and whether the study can detect one that small. If it cannot, that is worth knowing before fieldwork rather than after.

raised_when: outcome_missingness is one of “High — over 20%” or “Not yet established”
message: A substantial share of outcomes is expected to be missing, or the share has not been established. A complete-case analysis assumes those missing are unrelated to the outcome, which is rarely true and cannot be tested from the records that are present.
prompt: Ask what the analysis will do with missing outcomes — complete cases, multiple imputation, or a model for the missingness — and what the estimate becomes if those missing did worse than those observed.

message: The baseline rate and variability are assumed rather than sourced. Every figure in the sizing calculation rests on them.
prompt: Ask what happens to the required sample if the baseline is a third higher or lower than assumed. If the answer changes the design, the estimate needs a source.

raised_when: nhst_multiplicity is “Several outcomes with no plan”
message: Several outcomes will be tested with no stated adjustment or hierarchy. The chance of at least one spurious positive rises with each one.
prompt: Ask which single outcome the decision rests on, and whether the others are secondary or exploratory. Record that before the data arrive.

raised_when: nhst_icc is one of “Assumed without a source” or “Not yet obtained”
message: The design is clustered but the intracluster correlation is assumed or absent. The required number of clusters is sensitive to this value.
prompt: Ask for the required sample across a range of plausible correlations rather than at one value, and whether the design still works at the pessimistic end.

raised_when: nhst_sequential is “Yes, with no stated adjustment”
message: Interim analyses are planned with no stated adjustment. Repeatedly testing and stopping on significance inflates the error rate the design is meant to control.
prompt: Ask for a spending function or a formal stopping rule, agreed before the first look at the data.

message: The sizing rests on a single value for each input. Variance, baseline and correlation are all estimates, so one number implies more certainty about the design than exists.
prompt: Ask for the sample size across a range for each key input, and which input the answer is most sensitive to.

raised_when: bayes_prior_source is “Not yet established” or bayes_elicitation_protocol is “Informal discussion, no protocol”
message: The prior has no stated source, or rests on informal discussion rather than a documented elicitation. At small sample sizes the prior supplies much of the posterior, so an unexaminable prior makes the finding unexaminable.
prompt: Ask whether previous evaluations could supply the prior instead, and if expert judgement is the only option, whether a structured elicitation such as SHELF is practicable — individual judgements taken before group discussion, with the basis recorded.

raised_when: bayes_decision_threshold is one of “Not yet considered” or “Proposed, not yet agreed” and bayes_rope is “Not yet considered”
message: Neither a decision threshold nor a region of practical equivalence has been agreed. Without one the posterior cannot be turned into a decision, and the analysis reduces to reporting an interval.
prompt: Ask those making the decision what size of effect would change it, and what size they would treat as too small to matter. Those two answers are what the analysis reports against.

raised_when: bayes_prior_source is one of “From previous evaluations of similar interventions” or “From structured expert elicitation” and bayes_prior_share is one of “Not yet considered” or “Expected to be small, not yet checked”
message: An informative prior is in use but its contribution to the posterior has not been quantified. Where the prior supplies most of the answer, the finding largely restates what was assumed — and a Bayesian analysis chosen to rescue an underpowered study will do exactly that without saying so.
prompt: Ask for the prior's effective sample size alongside the actual one, and for the posterior under a deliberately sceptical prior. If the conclusion changes, the study is reporting its assumptions.

raised_when: outcome_missingness is one of “High — over 20%” or “Not yet established”
message: A substantial share of outcomes is expected to be missing, or the share has not been established. A prior sharpens the posterior whether or not the missingness is handled, so an informative prior can make an estimate look more precise than the observed records support.
prompt: Ask for the missingness mechanism to be stated and modelled alongside the outcome, and for the posterior under an assumption that those missing differ from those observed. Precision bought from the prior is not evidence about the people whose outcomes were never seen.

message: No prior sensitivity analysis is planned. This is the standard reviewer challenge and a stated regulatory expectation.
prompt: Ask which alternative priors will be run — at minimum a sceptical one and a weakly informative one — and agree them before the data are seen.

raised_when: bayes_audience_calibration is “Yes, with no simulation planned”
message: The audience expects frequentist error-rate guarantees but no simulation is planned to provide them. A posterior probability does not answer a question about long-run error rates.
prompt: Ask whether the operating characteristics can be simulated — the false positive and false negative rates the design would show across repeated hypothetical studies — or whether the audience can be brought to a probabilistic answer.

message: The design stops early on accumulating data without simulated operating characteristics. Adaptive stopping is a real advantage of the approach, and its behaviour has to be established rather than assumed.
prompt: Ask for simulations across a range of true effects, including no effect, showing how often the rule stops early and what it concludes when it does.
